description.narrative: Programmet styrs av visionen i UN Women's Global Strategic Plan 2022-2025: "Uppnå jämställdhet, stärkandet av alla kvinnor och flickor, och förverkligandet av sina mänskliga rättigheter”. Insatsen är tänkt att resultera i: - Avlägsnande av strukturella och normativa hinder för kvinnors jämställdhet och värdighet, och respekt för kvinnors och flickors rätt att leva fritt från våld, inklusive de som är relaterade till våld och fördrivning. - Demokratiska institutioner som kommer att säkerställa kvinnors deltagande och ansvarighet mekanismer och processer som införts för att effektivt komma till rätta med kränkningar av rättigheterna för kvinnor och flickor. – Kvinnor, deras organisationer och civilsamhället blir mer aktiva och effektiva i hävda sina rättigheter, ställa regeringen till svars och delta i förvaltningen processer och strukturer. – En ekonomi, ekonomiska möjligheter och sociala skyddsinstitutioner som är strukturerad för att vara mer genuskänslig och inkluderande. – Klimatförändringar och miljöförstörande åtgärder som är mer genus lyhörda och som säkerställer kvinnors deltagande och fördelar. UN Women Ethiopia Country Offices program bidrar till FN:s delade mål för att stödja Etiopiens regering att uppnå sin hållbarhet utveckling och humanitära prioriteringar och åtaganden för 2030 års utveckling Dagordning. Det finns fyra strategiska prioriteringar i FN:s hållbarhet Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2020-2025 som tar upp multidimensionell fattigdom, ojämlikheter, social utslagning och marginalisering, med en fokusera på ungdomar, kvinnor och flickor; stödja övergången till en inkluderande och diversifierad ekonomi; fördjupa Etiopiens demokratiska övergång och främja fred; och främja en grön och motståndskraftig ekonomi.

The programme is guided by the vision in UN Women's global Strategic Plan 2022-2025: ‘Achieve gender equality, the empowerment of all women and girls, and the fulfilment of their human rights’. The intervention is supposed to result in: - Removal of structural and normative barriers to women’s equality and dignity, and respect for women’s and girls’ right to live free of violence, including in those related to violence and displacement. - Democratic institutions that will ensure women’s participation, and accountability mechanisms and processes put in place to effectively redress violations of the rights of women and girls. - Women, their organizations and civil society being more active and effective in claiming their rights, holding government to account and participating in governance processes and structures. - An economy, economic opportunities and social protection institutions that are structured to be more gender responsive and inclusive. - Climate change and environmental degradation measures that are more gender responsive and that ensure the participation and benefiting of women. The UN Women Ethiopia Country Office’s program contributes to the UN’s shared goals in supporting the Government of Ethiopia to achieve its sustainable development and humanitarian priorities, and commitments to the 2030 Development Agenda. There are four strategic priorities in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2020-2025 that address multidimensional poverty, inequalities, social exclusion, and marginalization, with a focus on youth, women and girls; supporting the transition to an inclusive and diversified economy; deepening Ethiopia’s democratic transition and promoting peace; and promoting a green and resilient economy.

The programmatic priorities are centred around the four following results pillars aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development 9 Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2020-2025) to address multidimensional poverty, inequalities, social exclusion, and marginalization, with a focus on youth, women, and girls :
1. All people in Ethiopia enjoy the rights and capabilities to realize their potential, in equality and with dignity. 2. All people in Ethiopia live in a cohesive, just, inclusive, and democratic society. 3. All people in Ethiopia benefit from an inclusive, resilient, and sustainable economy. 4. All people in Ethiopia live in a society resilient to environmental risks and adapted to climate change.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Below results are extracted from the Annual Report for 2024 (UM2021/39631/ADDI-77), which was due 30 June 2025.
Overall, UN Women has continued to be instrumental in supporting the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) to enhance its gender equality and womens empowerment frameworks. A significant achievement is the development of a new National Policy on Gender Equality and Womens Empowerment, which is set to replace the outdated National Policy on Ethiopian Women (1993). UN Womens technical support and advocy for its accelerated review and approval was instrumental for the draft policy finally reaching the stage for submission to the Prime Ministers Office for endorsement in 2024. The same goes for Ethiopia's National Action Plan (NAP) on Women, Peace, and Security (WPS), which UN Womens contributions has contributed to shape and process. Extensive nationwide consultations were held during 2024, with the first draft of the National Action Plan being shared among federal ministries in September 2024. Regrettably, just as the above mentioned National Policy on Gender Equality and Womens Empowerment, this NAP is still pending endorsement in December 2025, for reasons beyond the control of UN Women.
Further, during 2024, UN Women made significant progress in institutionalizing gender mainstreaming efforts across different regions. Resulting in the Gender Strategy and Coordination Frameworks for the Tigray, Somali, and Amhara regions were finalized in 2024. These frameworks empower regional Bureaus to lead gender equality initiatives, reinforcing accountability and coordination in implementing gender-sensitive programs and mainstreaming gender in all humanitarians, development, and peace initiatives.
In the Humanitarian action, UN Women strengthened the coordination of gender in humanitarian action through steering the work of the National Gender in Humanitarian Action (GiHA) working group and especially its decentralization to selected regional humanitarian hotspots like Tigray, Amhara, Afar, Somali and Oromia regions.
Through sustained capacity building on Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB) supported by UN Women, three key federal ministries; Agriculture; Justice, and Youth and Sport have demonstrated significant progress in integrating gender considerations into their planning and budgeting processes. For example, Ministry of Agriculture included gender and sex-disaggregated targets in its two-year budget proposal planning to support more than five million women-headed households in agriculture and horticulture; beyond 47,000 women in urban agriculture and around 90,000 women in securing land title deeds. Ministry of Justice set a target to improve investigation and sentencing rates for crimes against women and children from 85% to 100% by 2025, with corresponding budget allocations proposed. Ministry of Youth and Sport committed to achieving 50% representation of women in leadership positions by 2025. These developments reflect strengthened institutional ownership of gender equality goals and increased political will to allocate resources for womens empowerment which shows institutional change resulting from UN Womens advocacy and capacity developments for GRB.
Further, in 2024, UN Women provided essential services to more than 4000 ex-combatants and survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Conflict-Related Sexual Violence (CRSV). Among them, almost 1000 women and girls received multi-sectoral services across various regions, including Addis Ababa, Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Somali and Tigray. These services have enabled survivors to regain a sense of safety, access justice, and rebuild their lives, while also strengthening regional capacities to respond effectively to GBV and CRSV cases.
The implementation of the "SASA!" community mobilization strategy in Oromia, supported by UN Women and AWSAD, is reported to have led to significant shifts in attitudes and behaviors toward violence against women and girls. Over four years, the strategy fostered equitable social norms and built strong community resistance to violence, resulting in major improvements such as increased rejection of VAW, awareness of the link between violence and HIV, assistance to survivors, and speaking out against VAW, demonstrating the power of sustained community engagement in driving meaningful behavioral and social change.
Finally, in 2024, over 360 women leaders across Amhara, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia, and Tigray benefited from targeted capacity-building, mentorship, and leadership development, resulting in measurable gains in knowledge, skills and confidence. In this way, UN Women significantly contributed to building a more cohesive, just, inclusive, and democratic society in Ethiopia by strengthening womens leadership and institutional capacity through strategic partnerships with federal and regional governments and civil society.
